name: Enoxaparin
reviewed_by: William Gregory M. Rivero, MD, FPCP, DPSN
drafted_by: AI-assisted draft (Claude) for review by Dr. W. Rivero
summary: Enoxaparin exposure rises in kidney impairment. The US label reduces doses when creatinine clearance (CrCl) is below 30 mL/min, mostly to once-daily regimens, and recommends no adjustment at CrCl 30 mL/min or higher.

bands.recommendation: Usual dosing (label: no adjustment at CrCl 50 to 80).
No dose adjustment (label: CrCl 30 to <50 and 50 to 80); observe for bleeding.

Prophylaxis (abdominal surgery, hip or knee replacement, acutely ill medical patients): 30 mg SC once daily. Deep vein thrombosis (DVT) treatment, unstable angina/non-Q-wave myocardial infarction (MI): 1 mg/kg SC once daily. ST-elevation MI under 75 years: 30 mg IV bolus plus 1 mg/kg SC, then 1 mg/kg SC once daily; 75 years and older: 1 mg/kg SC once daily, no bolus (label).
Label severe-impairment regimens (CrCl <30) as above; no separate guidance below 15. Bleeding risk high: specialist input.

hd: No dosing in label. A single-dose study showed about 2-fold higher exposure in hemodialysis patients (label). Insufficient data: avoid or use with specialist input (consider anti-factor Xa monitoring).
pd: No data in label. Insufficient data: specialist input.
crrt: No data in label. Insufficient data: specialist input.
monitoring: Signs of bleeding in all kidney impairment; platelet count (heparin-induced thrombocytopenia); potassium (hyperkalemia reported in renal failure) (label).

pediatric.approved_ages: Safety and effectiveness not established in pediatric patients; not approved for neonates or infants (label).
pediatric.neonates: Neonates: not approved. Multiple-dose vials contain benzyl alcohol (gasping syndrome risk in premature neonates) (label).
pediatric.egfr_equation: Bedside Schwartz: eGFR (mL/min/1.73 m2) = 0.413 x height (cm) / serum creatinine (mg/dL)

adult: Abbreviations SC (subcutaneous) and IV (intravenous) in band text are not expanded; rendered panel shows only the summary as prose. Decide whether to spell out.
Label is silent on dialysis dosing; many units use unfractionated heparin instead. No PubMed-verified dosing source for enoxaparin in dialysis was added.
pediatric: Pediatric enoxaparin is widely used off-label with anti-Xa monitoring; label says not established, so nothing is drafted. Needs a verified pediatric source if Dr. Rivero wants it.
